The Exodus

    About this map

    A style study for the project's Bible maps, after Eilers Sunday School Map No. 5, The Exodus (A. H. Eilers & Co., St. Louis), redrawn from open data. Where Eilers drew one confident route, this map shows what is known and what is guessed.

    What we kept from Eilers

    • Flat tints for each kingdom and people, with the seas left as paper
    • Water lines along the coasts, and hachured relief
    • Widely spaced capitals for lands and wildernesses
    • A red route with numbered camps, and a table of the camps
    • A "?" after places whose location is uncertain
    • A grid with an index of places keyed to it

    What we changed

    • Labels never overlap. More appear as you zoom in.
    • Type is never smaller than 11 pixels on screen
    • Borders are drawn as lines as well as tints, so they don't depend on color
    • Only camps with a proposed site are plotted, and the route is dashed where the camps between are unknown
    • Mount Sinai is shown at each of its main proposed sites, not one

    How it was made

    • Land, water and relief come from elevation data, and the Nile from Natural Earth. The Dead Sea is drawn at its old shoreline.
    • The camps are those of Numbers 33, at the site OpenBible.info's sources favour. Most are uncertain; the table of camps gives each one's proposed site and certainty.
    • The route joins the plotted camps along the easiest ground between them. It is a picture of the order of the camps, not a claim about the path.
    • Lands are approximate, drawn around their towns. The roads follow standard reconstructions through the places that mark them.
    • Places are the towns named in Genesis to Deuteronomy that OpenBible.info can locate. Places scored below 500 out of 1,000 are marked "?".
    • Names are spelled as in this project's Open Plain English Translation.

    Sources

    • Places: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data, CC BY 4.0
    • Elevation: AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM, GMTED2010, ETOPO1)
    • Style: the Eilers Sunday School wall maps, published before 1931
    • Rivers: Natural Earth (public domain)
